text:
mike: Proposal — make trace TTL env-aware and let services opt into longer hot retention. idea: dev=7d, staging=30d, prod=90d by default, with per-service overrides for high-card services.

anya: strong +1 for defaults, but we need a path for short-term compliance exceptions (some customers want 1y). can we have a tenant-level override?

kevin: concern: hot storage is expensive. if a service opts into 90d hot we should require sampling increase + joi n background cold move to cheaper object store after 14d. otherwise unit costs explode.

emily: agree with kevin. we also need to preserve span-level continuity for trace-based alerting (not just raw spans). archived traces should be queryable via async recall API.

ops-sarah: operational note — search & dashboards expect a few weeks of hot traces for latency percentiles. if we drop below 30d hot we break the SLO dashboards for many teams.

mike: ack. how about: prod default 90d hot, with automatic cold-migration after 14d for spans that are low-cardinality or marked "archivable" by sampler. add request to the console to pin a trace to hot for 30d if needed.

kevin: technical nit — how do we mark spans? sampler-level tag? otoh adding per-span flags is heavier on agents. maybe add a service-level metadata field "trace_retention_policy: hot-90|hot-30|cold-only" and apply exporter routing.

anya: that sounds workable. UI needs to surface what services are currently on hot retention and who approved it (audit trail). legal will want the change log.

otel-bot: FYI: current OTLP exporter config doesn't have a retention_policy field. example config we'd expect: ```yaml exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: otel.redwood:4317
    sample_rate: 0.25
    retention_policy: "hot-90"
```

emily: any thoughts about changing sampling to satisfy cost constraints? maybe adaptive sampling that raises sample_rate for errors/transactions above threshold, and lowers for background jobs.

kevin: yes, adaptive sampling + prefix/KV cache for traces reduces token-like costs. also propose default downsample for spans older than 7d when moving to cold, keep 1 trace per 1000 for low-value flows.

ops-sarah: What about queries that need full fidelity for debugging incidents? we should expose an on-demand rehydrate API that copies from cold back into hot for a given trace id and sets TTL. needs rate limits and audit.

mike: rehydrate API is a must. we can gate it behind a console action + API key with approval. add quota cost so teams can't abuse it.

anya: rollout plan idea: 1) add retention_policy field to exporter and service metadata (beta) 2) implement routing + cold store + rehydrate 3) opt-in console toggle for first 30d 4) auto-enforce defaults after 90 days if no opt-out.

kevin: one more: metrics we need to decide policy = hot storage cost delta, query latency impact, % of traces rehydrated. dashboard tile needed: "hot retention cost by service".

emily: also add regression alert for telemetry coverage — if sampling changes reduce error-derived traces, we should flag potential blind spots.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: retention-policy-service v0.3 -> canary on prod-1 at 2026-03-19T14:05Z.

ops-sarah: can we include a migration playbook in the PR? steps to rollback if dashboards break.

mike: yes, I'll draft the playbook and a short RFC. thanks all — next step: kevin & emily pair on exporter schema, anya + ops-sarah draft console UX + audit flow. meeting tomorrow 10am? :calendar: 

kevin: 10am works for me. :thumbsup:

anya: adding RFC to docs repo after call. :spiral_notepad:

emily: will sketch sampling knobs.

otel-bot: Note: automatic retention enforcement will start 2026-06-01 if not configured otherwise.
